paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar Chisma. (a) Mishnah, end of Avot, chapter 3; Terumot 3:5; Yoma 19b; Bava Metzia 7:5; Nega'im 7:2, 13:3; Mikvaot 8:3.

(b) Called Chisma because he was stopped, Vayikra Rabbah, Acharei, section 23: Heilprin describes the request as concerning blessings such as the seven wedding blessings [this midrash illustrates its point with mourners’ blessings, then has Elazar asked to lead the Shema and prayer]. Midrash Chazit, “Like a rose among thorns”: blessings and leading the Shema. “They call you Rabbi for nothing,” they said; hence Chisma, from “Do not muzzle an ox,” until he studied with Akiva. Mattanot Kehunnah: Chisma means strengthened. The Midrash seems so: they named him after he knew how to lead the Shema and prayer. Why give a derogatory name? He also has a ruling on muzzling, Hassokher et Hapo'alim. Maimonides says he appears only in Terumot, chapter 3, but also Nega'im, chapters 7, 13, and Bava Metzia 7:5. Heilprin reads ben Chisma in those places [the checked Mishnah texts in Nega’im and Bava Metzia read Chisma]. Yet the above suggests Chisma was his own epithet: the Midrash says “Elazar once came to a place,” asked to lead, etc., not “Elazar ben Chisma came.” Understand. Tosafot Yom Tov, end of Avot, chapter 3, likewise suggests this.

(c) A great astronomer and geometer, estimating how many drops are in the sea, yet without food or clothing. Gamliel wanted to appoint him head to provide livelihood. Chisma and his fellow appointee did not come at first. Gamliel told them, “I am giving you servitude,” Horayot 10a; Sifrei, Devarim, “I commanded your judges.” End of Rosh Hashanah: he led prayer.

(d) He spoke to Eliezer ben Yaakov, who spoke to him, Pesachim 32a. Chananya ben Antigonus in his name. His colleague Yochanan ben Gudgeda (see there); Yehudah ben Beroka [the checked Bavli names Yochanan ben Beroka]. They went to greet Yehoshua at Peki'in, Chagigah 3. Yochanan ben Nuri; Yose ben Meshullam in his time. (See Shimon ben Menasya.)
